paragraphs: Organizations must protect data, monitor resources, record actions, evaluate configurations, find security issues, and demonstrate compliance.

bullets: RECORD → Maintain evidence of events and actions
PROVE → Produce compliance evidence and reports

sections.title: Security vs. Governance vs. Compliance

entries.title: Security
paragraphs: Protect systems, resources, and data.

entries.title: Governance
paragraphs: Establish and maintain control over how cloud resources are managed.

entries.title: Compliance
paragraphs: Meet applicable legal, regulatory, industry, and organizational requirements.

sections.callout: Security, governance, and compliance overlap, but they are not interchangeable.

sections.title: Benefits of Cloud Security and Security Logs
paragraphs: AWS provides security capabilities at cloud scale, including encryption, monitoring, threat and vulnerability findings, centralized visibility, and recorded events. Cloud security logs help investigations reconstruct actions, changes, events, and resource behavior.
bullets: Know which service produces the needed evidence
Protect both moving and stored data
Use customer-configured controls under the shared responsibility model
sections.callout: The value of a log depends on whether the question asks about performance, an API action, or resource configuration.

sections.title: AWS Artifact
paragraphs: AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS security and compliance documents and certain agreements.
sections.callout: ARTIFACT → AWS COMPLIANCE PAPERWORK AND EVIDENCE

entries.title: Geographic Locations
paragraphs: Requirements may depend on country, jurisdiction, Region, or where data is handled.

entries.title: Industries
paragraphs: Healthcare, financial services, retail, and other industries can have different obligations based on the information they handle.

entries.title: AWS Services
paragraphs: Not every service has identical compliance eligibility or characteristics. Customers must verify whether a service fits their workload's requirements.
entries.memoryHook: AWS service does not automatically mean every compliance requirement is satisfied.

sections.title: Encryption Options

entries.title: Encryption in Transit
paragraphs: Protects data while it moves between clients, services, systems, or networks.

entries.title: Encryption at Rest
paragraphs: Protects data while stored in databases, disks, or storage systems.

sections.callout: Is the data moving or sitting?

sections.title: Services Customers Use to Secure AWS Resources

entries.title: Amazon Inspector
paragraphs: Identifies software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure in supported workloads.

entries.title: Amazon GuardDuty
paragraphs: Threat detection that analyzes relevant AWS data sources for suspicious or potentially malicious activity.

entries.title: AWS Security Hub
paragraphs: Centralizes security findings and helps manage cloud security posture.
entries.memoryHook: Gather security findings in one place.

entries.title: AWS Shield
paragraphs: Helps protect AWS workloads against distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.

entries.title: Amazon CloudWatch
paragraphs: Monitors resources and applications through metrics, logs, alarms, and operational visibility.

entries.title: AWS CloudTrail
paragraphs: Records AWS account and API activity for auditing, governance, security investigation, and event history.

entries.title: AWS Audit Manager
paragraphs: Helps continually collect evidence and organize it against audit frameworks to support audit preparation and compliance assessment.

entries.title: AWS Config
paragraphs: Records and evaluates AWS resource configurations, configuration history, changes, and compliance with rules.
entries.memoryHook: How is or was it configured?

entries.title: Access Reports
paragraphs: Provide visibility into permissions and access-related information for governance and review.

table.caption: Match the scenario to the service or concept

entries.title: Artifact vs. CloudTrail
paragraphs: AWS compliance documentation → Artifact. Audit account and API actions → CloudTrail.

entries.title: Inspector vs. GuardDuty
paragraphs: Find vulnerabilities → Inspector. Detect threats and suspicious activity → GuardDuty.

entries.title: GuardDuty vs. Security Hub
paragraphs: Detect potential threats → GuardDuty. Centralize security findings → Security Hub.

entries.title: Shield vs. GuardDuty
paragraphs: DDoS protection → Shield. Threat detection → GuardDuty.

entries.title: CloudWatch vs. CloudTrail
paragraphs: Metrics, monitoring, and alarms → CloudWatch. Who performed an AWS action → CloudTrail.

entries.title: CloudTrail vs. Audit Manager vs. Config
paragraphs: Who did it → CloudTrail. Organize audit evidence → Audit Manager. How is or was it configured → Config.

entries.title: Transit vs. Rest
paragraphs: Moving data → Encryption in transit. Stored data → Encryption at rest.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Location or industry changes rules → Compliance requirements
